ety.text: From Middle English deyen, probably from Old Norse deyja, from Proto-Germanic *dawjaną (“to die”). Displaced native Old English sweltan, whence Modern English swelt, and Old English steorfan, whence modern starve.

From Middle English dee, from Old French de (Modern French dé), from Latin datum, from datus (“given”), the past participle of dō (“to give”), from Proto-Indo-European *deh₃- (“to lay out, to spread out”). Doublet of datum. Replaced Old English tasul, tesul (“die”), from Latin tessella (“die, cube”).
Borrowed from Latin die (“[in a] day”), locative of Latin dies (“day”).

senses.d: To stop living; to become dead; to undergo death.
ex:
Returne with ſpeed, time paſſeth ſwift away,
Our life is fraile, and we may dye to day.

The cheeks drop in; the body bows;
Man dies: nor is there hope in dust: […]

senses.d: followed by of as an indication of direct cause; general use
ex: He died of malaria.

"What did she die of, Work'us?" said Noah.
"Of a broken heart, some of our old nurses told me," replied Oliver[…].

senses.d: followed by from as an indication of direct cause; general use, though somewhat more common in the context of medicine or the sciences
ex: He died from heart failure.
She lived several weeks; but afterwards she died from epilepsy, to which malady she had been previously subject.

senses.d: followed by for; often expressing wider contextual motivations, though sometimes indicating direct causes
ex: He died for the one he loved.
Less than three days later, Johnson lapsed into a coma in his jail cell and died for lack of insulin.

senses.d: followed by with as an indication of direct cause
ex: And there were some who died with fevers, which at some seasons of the year was very frequent in the land.

senses.d: followed by to as an indication of direct cause (like from)
ex: I can't believe I just died to a turret!

senses.d: followed by with as an indication of manner
ex: She died with dignity.

senses.d: to die in a certain form.
ex: Will I die a happy man?

senses.d: To (stop living and) undergo (a specified death).
ex: He died a hero's death.
They died a thousand deaths.

senses.d: To lose or be eliminated from a game, particularly with a deathlike animation.
ex: Whenever my brother dies, he ragequits.
Oh look, I just died.[…]I missed that jump again! That was dumb! Hey, I just died on the same freakin' Zinger.

A mold for forming metal or plastic objects.

An oblong chip fractured from a semiconductor wafer engineered to perform as an independent device or integrated circuit.
ex: The number of dies per wafer is basically the area of the wafer divided by the area of the die.

senses.d: Any small cubical or square body.
An isohedral polyhedron, usually a cube, with numbers or symbols on each side and thrown in games of chance.
ex: Most dice are six-sided.
I rolled the die and moved 2 spaces on the board.

senses.d: That which is, or might be, determined, by a throw of the die; hazard; chance.
ex: […]For th'equall die of warre he well did know.

ety.text: From German Diesel, named after inventor Rudolf Diesel, who developed a heavy-duty engine in Germany (1892–1897) and perfected it throughout his life.

senses.d: A fuel derived from petroleum (or other oils) but heavier than gasoline/petrol. Used to power diesel engines which burn this fuel using the heat produced when air is compressed.
ex: They were chagrined to see that the price of diesel had climbed past six dollars a gallon.

senses.d: A vehicle powered by a diesel engine.
ex: His next truck will be a diesel.

senses.d: A rider who has an even energy output, without bursts of speed.
Synonym of snakebite and black.
A particular cannabis hybrid.
To ignite a substance by using the heat generated by compression.

For a spark-ignition internal combustion engine to continue running after the electrical current to the spark plugs has been turned off. This occurs when there's enough heat in the combustion chamber to ignite the air and fuel mixture without a spark, the same way that heat and pressure cause ignition in a diesel engine.
ex: The only reason the VW bug has a solenoid is to prevent it from dieseling.

senses.d: The food and beverage a person or animal consumes.
ex: The diet of the giant panda consists mainly of bamboo.
It is common policy to order no more diet than will be used within one month.

senses.d: A controlled regimen of food and drink choices, as to gain or lose weight or otherwise influence health.
ex: He's been on a diet since he found out that he has coronary atherosclerosis.
The doctor put me on a low-salt diet.

senses.d: Any habitual intake or consumption.
ex: He's been reading a steady diet of nonfiction for the last several years.

senses.d: Containing less fat, salt, sugar, or calories than normal, or claimed to have such.
ex: diet soda

senses.d: Having certain traits subtracted.
ex: You folks reduce it to the bible only as being authoritative, impoverishing the faith. "Christianity Lite", diet Christianity for those who can't handle the Whole Meal.

senses.d: To modify one's food and beverage intake so as to decrease or increase body weight or influence health.
ex: I've been dieting for six months, and I've lost some weight.

senses.d: To regulate the food of (someone); to put on a diet.
ex: they will diet themselves, feed and live alone.
When all signs of effusion, dulness, pain, œgophony, and cough had disappeared he was dieted, stimulated, and tonicked.

senses.d: To eat; to take one's meals.
ex: Let him[…]diet in such places, where there is good company of the nation, where he travelleth.

senses.d: To cause to take food; to feed.
ex: But partly led to diet my revenge […].

senses.d: A council or assembly of leaders; a formal deliberative assembly.
ex: the National Diet of Japan
They were given representation in some important diet committees.

senses.d: A session of exams.
ex: Normally the diet begins towards the end of April.

senses.d: A criminal proceeding in court.

senses.d: A prescribed meal plan setting out how the inhabitants of an institution (such as a prison, hospital etc.) should be fed, and on what foods.
ex: “Do I understand that he asked for more, after he had eaten the supper allotted by the dietary?” “He did, sir,” replied Bumble.
